column1: # Scoped item-description grammar; never global substring replacements.
# Captures: s=recursive item phrase, e=recursive predicate,
# f=complete non-liquid food ingredient, l=complete liquid food ingredient,
# v=descriptor color, j=complete dye-material list, o=craft profession,
# c=count, a=shared image elements, k=printed procedural WORD,
# q=complete quoted prose. Repeated captures are numbered in target order.
# retain the native producer graph, RTTI owners, switches, RAW leaves and
# dependent artwork/writing/instrument generators for the installed PE.
# Material, gem-cut, creature and item names remain in the existing tables.
# The item, object and artwork builders share nominal predicates as well as
# decoration predicates. This includes every image/rendition quality and
# material combination, and the object's color/quality description.
# Location captions, used only inside an identified item detail panel.
# Statue and figurine captions share the artwork subject grammar, including named
# creatures, their trailing species, quantities and multiple depicted figures.
# Order is material qualifier + depicted subject + item noun. The shared
# qualifier owns the material suffix, including bone and wood conventions.
# Memorial captions and the noun in "This is a memorial to ..." share the
# same person slot. The item parser unwraps quality/wear marks before these
# terms, so a closing mark cannot become part of the commemorated name.
# Native item quality and maker suffixes, shared by ordinary items and artifacts.
